newsitem.title: GERMANY: German autobahn speeds up with faster cars.
newsitem.headline: German autobahn speeds up with faster cars.

text.p: German drivers are putting their feet down harder on the accelerator than they were a decade ago, taking advantage of extensive stretches of autobahn without any speed limit, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The average speed on stretches of motorway without speed limits increased to 134 kmh (83 mph) in 1995 compared to 120 kmh in 1981 and one in six motorists travelled at speeds higher than 155 kmh (97 mph) in 1995, Bild newspaper said.
There are several thousand km (miles) of motorway in Germany with no speed limit.

Bild said one reason for the increase in average speeds was a growing number of powerful cars. Nearly 26 percent of the cars registered in Germany are now capable of exceeding 180 kmh, up from 17 percent in 1989.

German carmakers Porsche, Mercedes-Benz and BMW regularly fend off efforts by some politicians in Bonn to restrict speed on motorways, arguing the high-speed image helps them sell their cars around the world.
There were 13,714 serious accidents on motorways in 1995 and excess speed was cited as the cause in 20 percent of cases.
